## 固定收益市場開篇主論述

9月21日油價單日大跌，緩解先前將殖利率推上多年高點的部分通膨壓力，美國公債除前端外普遍上漲；聯準會官員的發言則使政策敏感的2年期殖利率守在4.75%附近。10年期殖利率下跌4.5個基點至4.952%，5年期下降2.9個基點至4.828%，30年期下跌4.2個基點至5.285%；2年期反而微升0.3個基點至4.748%，2年與10年期利差收窄4.8個基點至20.4個基點。

市場走勢凸顯投資人對眼前能源壓力緩解與聯準會較長期政策難題的不同判斷。外交前景改善，加上跡象顯示部分海灣出口仍經由荷莫茲海峽運出，削弱供應稀缺溢價，WTI期貨下跌8.22%至$92.06，布蘭特原油下跌7.46%至$96.12。然而，海峽可觀測到的航運量仍遠低於戰前常態。芝加哥聯準銀行總裁Austan Goolsbee與聖路易聯準銀行總裁Alberto Musalem分別指出，不能逕自忽視持續性的供給衝擊。今年沒有投票權的Musalem更進一步表示，目前3.75%至4%的聯邦基金利率區間仍屬寬鬆，可能需要繼續升息。

美債漲勢主要來自實質殖利率下降。10年期實質殖利率下跌6個基點至2.617%，10年期損益兩平通膨率卻上升1.5個基點至2.335%。這項分解顯示，隨著油價回落，投資人持有較長天期債券所要求的實質補償降低，但並未認定基礎通膨風險已經消失。芝加哥聯準銀行全國活動指數也支持成長轉弱的一面：8月指數由修正後的0.08降至-0.04，不及0.2的預測值。

風險資產將能源價格下跌視為利多，而非需求示警。Meta的Muse人工智慧代理程式初期採用情況良好，重新提振晶片需求的樂觀預期，帶動標普500指數上漲1.49%、Nasdaq 100上漲2.83%，費城半導體指數更大漲4.29%。高收益債利差大致持平，投資級、高收益及新興市場債券基金的單日報酬均為正。週一因此呈現長天期利率部位上漲與風險偏好強勁並存的格局，而非資金逃離信用市場。

不過，前端仍反映要求甚高的政策路徑。2年期殖利率較2月低點已上升約140個基點，期貨定價顯示未來一年聯準會還將緊縮約80個基點。部分投資人開始主張，接近4.75%的殖利率已反映這條路徑的大部分幅度；但Goolsbee與Musalem的發言說明，市場尚不能把9月升息視為本輪升息循環的終點。收盤走勢因此明顯分化：油價下跌與經濟活動轉弱支撐中長天期美債，進一步升息的可能性則使2年期無法獲得同等提振。

## 油價緩解壓低實質殖利率，聯準會則使前端維持高檔

美債當日走勢延續聯準會自2023年以來首次升息後的曲線壓平。2年與30年期利差收窄4.5個基點至53.7個基點，近一個月累計收窄近50個基點。即使較長天期券種受惠於週一漲勢，5年期殖利率同期仍上升40.3個基點，2年期更上升51.1個基點。市場因此維持對隔夜利率高檔路徑的預期，同時降低對曲線較遠端所要求的部分補償。

油價是這波緩解行情最明確的催化劑。伊朗戰爭干擾出口並使通膨前景更複雜，布蘭特原油一度在$100以上交易，但連續第4天下跌後收於$96.12。美國總統Donald Trump表示，他可能願意在聯合國大會期間與伊朗總統Masoud Pezeshkian會面；衛星觀測則顯示，沙烏地阿拉伯從波斯灣裝載的貨量增加。外交與持續出口若能改善供應，便可降低債市眼前反映的能源溢價。

然而，實體運輸情況不如期貨走勢所呈現的那麼令人安心。週末僅17艘商品運輸船通過荷莫茲海峽，低於一週前的37艘，也遠不及2月28日戰爭爆發前每日通常約有125艘大型商船通行的水準。可追蹤船舶並未涵蓋全部流量：截至9月13日當週，共有22艘油輪、其中多數為超大型原油輪，載運4,200萬桶原油駛出海峽；沙烏地阿拉伯與伊拉克各占43%。部分油輪航行時關閉了應答器。

仍有貨物流出，有助解釋市場為何降低部分極端供應情境的定價；但可見航運量驟減，代表這條能源運輸路線依然容易再度受阻。自9月16日起，也未觀測到沙烏地阿拉伯原油從紅海沿岸的延布港裝載。因此，週一油價下跌雖減弱當前的通膨衝擊，卻不足以證明正常出口能力已經恢復。

Goolsbee的演說正面處理了這項區別。他指出，供給衝擊已變得更頻繁、更嚴重且更持久，削弱了將其視為一次性價格水準變動而不予理會的傳統理由。相較於需求過剩造成經濟過熱，聯準會不必以同樣激烈的方式回應；但當政策縮小總供給與總需求間的缺口時，恢復價格穩定仍可能需要付出就業、工資與成長下降的代價。

這項看法對通膨降溫成本的著眼點，與主席Kevin Warsh在9月決策後的說法不同。Warsh認為，中期而言，聯準會的充分就業與物價穩定目標並不相互牴觸，也不認同把通膨拉回2%必須傷害勞動市場。Goolsbee則把反覆出現的負面供給衝擊視為本質上痛苦的取捨：衝擊一旦持續，即使最初的價格上漲源自其他因素，貨幣緊縮仍須壓低需求。

Musalem在盤中稍晚提供了另一項更明確的鷹派政策訊號。他表示，強勁需求與反覆出現的供給因素都使通膨風險居高不下；若不進一步收緊政策，18個月後通膨大幅高於2%的可能性，將高於回到目標的可能性。他認為，及早採取漸進式升息，造成的干擾會小於等待後再被迫大幅調整。

Musalem估計，排除油價與其他供給因素後，基礎通膨可能高於目標約1個百分點，而且方向仍在惡化。7月個人消費支出通膨年增率為3.7%，高於2025年4月近期低點2.3%。他認為3.75%至4%的政策利率區間仍偏寬鬆，這一點格外重要，因為判斷並非只建立在油價衝擊之上。Musalem今年在聯邦公開市場委員會沒有投票權，也未指出下一次行動的會議或終端利率，但其偏好的政策方向十分明確。

市場的反應比單純否定這些警告更為細緻。2年期殖利率守在2024年以來最高水準附近；隨著原油下跌，能源衝擊迫使實質利率更大幅調整的風險下降，5年至30年期券種則普遍上漲。2年期殖利率為4.748%，也高於交換市場所反映的2027年9月政策利率約4.68%。這項正利差收益吸引了認為市場已反映另外3次升息的投資人；若通膨改善或聯準會實際升息次數較少，這些部位可望明顯受惠。

反方論點則是，過往升息循環的幅度經常超出投資人最初預期。美國銀行策略師指出，政策利率最終可能超過5%，尤其若官員持續認為現行設定的限制性不足。若外交失敗或出口路線惡化，油價也可能迅速反轉。因此，週一的殖利率曲線反映的是有條件的舒緩，而非市場已確信終端利率塵埃落定。

當日經濟數據小幅有利較長天期債券。8月芝加哥聯準銀行全國活動指數降至-0.04，低於0.2的預測值與7月修正後的0.08。指數並未顯示經濟嚴重萎縮，但在消費與勞動市場仍具韌性之際，進一步證實部分生產活動及整體經濟動能正在減弱。

國庫券標售顯示，最短天期的融資成本仍在上升。3個月期國庫券得標利率為4.015%，高於前次的3.970%與3.9999%的預測值；6個月期得標利率則由4.060%升至4.155%。這些結果符合市場幾乎不預期近期降息、且即使較長天期附息債殖利率下降，仍持續反映政策緊縮的格局。

## 全球央行從不同起點因應同一能源衝擊

加拿大、南韓與南非分別顯示，能源衝擊如何改變美國以外央行的政策考量。加拿大央行總裁Tiff Macklem表示，若通膨仍受控制，官員不希望壓抑成長；但也不願等到持續性壓力迫使央行升息得更快、更高。關鍵在於目前2.25%的政策利率能否使通膨回到2%，或仍需再升息一次。

加拿大整體通膨率大致維持在3%，主因是汽油價格。Macklem表示，若油價停留在$100附近，未來數月通膨可能小幅走高；他更重視影響是否會從燃料擴散，而非把最初的能源漲價本身視為足以升息的理由。加拿大央行將在10月貨幣政策報告中使用新的Prima預測模型，區分暫時性與較持久的價格變化，並評估不同情境。

貿易壓力使這項評估更加複雜。Macklem指出，美國新關稅直接影響的產品，約占加拿大對美商品出口的5%，因此第一輪總體衝擊有限；但政策不可預測，仍可能延後投資與招募。他估計，若關稅維持不變，第4季成長率可能減半至1%以下。加拿大面臨的不只是高通膨：太早升息可能加劇貿易引發的經濟放緩，太晚行動則可能讓能源壓力擴散。

在南韓，摩根大通認為政策利率高點可能超過該行原已高於市場共識的預測。該行預期11月、2月與5月各升息25個基點，使韓國央行利率由3%升至3.75%；市場預測中位數則為3.5%，並預期維持至2028年第2季。韓國央行8月預測僅隱含未來6個月再升息一次。

摩根大通經濟學家Seok Gil Park將利率高點的上行風險與半導體熱潮連結。他預估南韓經濟2026年成長3.8%、2027年成長3.3%，均高於韓國央行的3.3%與2.9%；第3季經濟則預計季增約1%，央行估值約為0.3%。企業投資已經受惠，但晶片業獲利能否擴散至供應商、工資與家庭需求，將決定通膨效應能持續多久。

韓元升值可降低進口成本；但若升值反映貿易條件改善與實質所得增加，其影響未必完全是通膨降溫。Park正觀察不含石油的核心製造品與個人服務價格，這些項目的月增幅仍然偏高。市場預期韓國央行10月22日按兵不動，10月聲明及11月預測將是下一項檢驗，顯示官員是否更加重視景氣熱潮向國內經濟擴散的效應。

南非則將於9月23日作出較近期的決策。摩根士丹利將預測由維持利率改為升息25個基點至7.25%，並把這次行動形容為保險，以免反覆的供給衝擊延後通膨回到南非儲備銀行3%的目標。這項主張並非基於目前通膨預期惡化，也沒有證據顯示能源壓力已廣泛傳至消費物價；理由在於油價若長期上漲，將壓低實質政策利率，並增加通膨預期最終失去錨定的機率。

美國銀行預期的升息序列更長，9月與11月將各升息25個基點，使附買回利率升至7.5%。該行把第4季平均通膨預測上調至5%，並預計2027年第1季觸及5.3%的高點。摩根士丹利則預測升息一次後，利率將在2027年全年維持不變。調查所示通膨預期實際上已由3.9%降至3.8%，雙方分歧因此集中在第二輪效應出現前，央行應多積極地防範油價風險。

同樣的張力遍及非洲。未來兩週開會的11家央行中，市場預期7家維持利率、3家升息、1家降息。奈及利亞先前通膨降溫雖創造一定空間，但近期燃料價格上漲可能使趨勢逆轉，預計將連續第3次會議把利率維持在26.5%。摩洛哥預計維持2.25%，埃及則可能讓19%的利率延續至年底。能源與食品在當地物價中的權重格外高；部分國家的消費物價籃子中，食品占比高達一半，而強烈的聖嬰現象又威脅收成。

印度債市則透過流動性、而非只靠政策利率，承受相關緊縮壓力。指標10年期公債殖利率前一週收於7.0686%，連續第5週上升；當週上升5個基點，過去4週累計約上升26個基點。印度儲備銀行已出售5,000億盧比較短天期公債，是2017年以來首次進行淨標售出售，另安排9月21日再出售2,500億盧比，下一個週一再出售2,500億盧比。

銀行先前透過一項特殊外匯動員計畫籌得$1,270億，產生的資金使銀行體系轉為流動性過剩，並將隔夜利率壓到政策走廊下限以下。出售債券因此具有貨幣控制目的，但在交易員上調升息預期之際，也增加供給並壓抑較長天期債券。

中國的匯率走向則相反。在岸人民幣一度升至每美元6.6950元，為2023年1月以來最強，並收於6.6955元，創2022年6月以來最強境內收盤價。中國人民銀行將中間價設在6.7487元，為2023年2月以來最強。雖然中間價仍比Reuters估值弱536點，但9月升值速度加快，且與市場預期的差距收窄，顯示官員對人民幣逐步走強的容忍度正在提高。

## AI融資考驗信用需求的深度與價格

SoftBank把原本可能成為超大型交易的籌資案具體化，推出$100億美元計價高順位無擔保債券，以及€10億、約合$11.5億的歐元債券。若按計畫規模完成，這將成為亞太及日本地區歷來最大宗非金融企業債發行，超越7-Eleven於2021年1月發行的$109.3億債券。

美元債分為3.5年、5.5年及7.5年期，歐元債則分為4年及6年期。交易預計9月24日定價、9月29日交割。募集資金將用於支付SoftBank追加投資OpenAI的第3期款$100億，該投資預計10月1日完成，其餘用於一般企業用途。這批債券將取代先前一筆已有擔保的$100億過橋融資。

交易規模使其意義不只是再度證明初級市場流動性充裕。SoftBank已承諾向OpenAI投資近$650億，2026年跨幣別發債近$150億，成為今年規模最大的非投資級債券借款人。由於美債殖利率與SoftBank信用利差同步上升，其2031年到期美元債殖利率由1月的6.7%升至9月稍早的8.2%。Fitch給予擬發行債券BB+評級，與S&P給予該公司的最高投機級評等一致。

這項結構把SoftBank部分OpenAI曝險由有擔保過橋融資轉為無擔保公開債務，雖可拓展到期結構，卻也把更多投資風險轉由債券持有人承擔。OpenAI決定今年不推動首次公開募股，也延後了SoftBank持股一項潛在的流動性來源。在AI相關借款異常龐大的一年之後，最終定價將顯示投資人針對這項集中度要求多少補償。

另一筆資料中心融資則呈現承擔興建風險的成本。由Goldman Sachs領銜的銀行團開始推銷約$11億Digital Drive非投資級債券。該專案位於維吉尼亞州Richmond附近，由Blue Owl Capital、Cedarwood Investment Group及PowerHouse Data Centers的關係企業贊助。初步討論的殖利率落在9%區間低端至中段，預計9月23日定價。

該專案76兆瓦的資訊科技容量將依據一紙15年、總值$29.4億的合約，全數出租給CoreWeave，預計2027年至2028年間開始營運。租約提供可見的收入來源，但設施正式啟用前，投資人仍須承擔施工、完工及承租人信用風險。指示性殖利率顯示，與AI客戶簽訂長期合約雖能協助取得融資，仍無法消除未完工專案所附帶的溢酬。

Fidelity International投資組合經理James Durance認為，科技業債務總量的成長本身就是風險。他管理的收益策略規模達$140億，當中科技業曝險一直維持在2%以下；他主張，該產業借款到2027年底可能具有系統性重要性。過去一年，全球科技債指標下跌約2.4%，較廣泛的全球綜合指數則下跌1.3%。他擔心的並非AI投資必然失敗，而是企業尚未證明龐大資本投入能否產生足夠報酬，長天期債務發行便已持續擴張。

同樣的資本密集程度也影響貨幣政策分析。歐洲央行管理委員會委員Fabio Panetta表示，市場估值包含對AI獲利能力的樂觀假設，一旦預期落空，價格可能劇烈修正。他估計，AI廣泛應用每年可使義大利生產力成長提高逾1個百分點，但其通膨效果取決於誰取得收益。預期所得提高可能強化消費並使通膨延續；自動化與就業不確定性也可能提高儲蓄，使通膨更早降溫。

週一股市走勢凸顯樂觀情境。Meta的Muse登上Apple App Store免費應用程式首位，帶動Meta股價上漲11%、Advanced Micro Devices上漲10%且市值突破$1兆、Intel上漲12%、Arm上漲17%。這波行情改善了AI融資的市場環境，卻也突顯股票估值、企業借款及投資支出日益依賴同一個科技週期。

信用需求並不限於AI。AMC Entertainment推出$20億非投資級債券與$8.5億槓桿貸款，並取得Deutsche Bank承諾提供的$11.2億第二順位留置權貸款，合計尋求近$40億資金以重整資本結構。債券初步發行殖利率位於9%區間低端。

AMC計畫償還2029年及2031年到期的定期貸款，以及AMC與Muvico發行、2029年到期的票據。6個月前，公司曾嘗試再融資，但因市場狀況不佳而失敗，之後被迫依賴與Deutsche Bank不良資產部門進行的$4.25億交易。這次融資條件改善以票房復甦為基礎：7月與8月營收年增42%至$13.3億，入場人次增加36%。截至6月30日，AMC仍有$37億企業借款，交易能否完成及其後利息負擔仍是核心問題。

儘管戰爭直接造成損害，卡達展現的主權融資地位強健得多。政府完成自去年11月以來首次公開國際債券發行，籌得$30億；5年期債券利差為美債加55個基點，10年期為美債加65個基點，兩者均較初步指引收窄約30個基點。訂單一度超過$77億，之後回落至約$68億。

需求反映卡達的AA評級、$5,800億主權財富基金，以及超過$700億外匯存底。這些緩衝與當期收入驟降同時存在：荷莫茲海峽受阻限制出貨，使液化天然氣出口收入由第1季的$90億降至第2季的$2億；單季預算赤字則創下$58億、相當於GDP 11.4%的紀錄。這筆交易顯示，即使營運衝擊嚴重，雄厚的累積資產仍可維持融資管道。

Nuveen也在籌備首筆英鎊債券，並搭配3筆美元債，以支應其£99億收購Schroders的部分資金。規劃中的英鎊債為5年期，募集資金將用於一般企業用途，包括支付收購現金對價；Nuveen此前已安排最高£31億的債務融資。連同SoftBank、AMC及Digital Drive專案，這批發行計畫顯示借款人正把握市場氣氛良好的交易日，處理各不相同的融資需求，而條件則依槓桿、擔保品及交易完成風險而大幅分化。

## 主權融資獎勵可信度，懲罰財政失序

智利是可信的財政與市場發展計畫吸引外資最鮮明的例子之一。非居民持有的披索計價主權債券在8月增加$7億，達到創紀錄的$210.4億，2026年初以來增幅達42%。截至3月，外國投資人持有本地主權債市場的15.6%，接近2024年底8%的兩倍。

資金流入同時伴隨財政改善。智利7月出現950億披索預算盈餘，一年前則為9,570億披索赤字。民營礦業收入成長79%，支出下降0.7%，年初至今支出也僅增加0.7%。財政部長Jorge Quiroz計畫把明年支出增幅限制在0%至1%，與拉丁美洲其他地區的財政惡化形成更明顯對比。

市場改革也支持資金配置。智利正尋求允許退休基金進行附買回與附賣回交易，以改善融資及次級市場流動性，並已就造市商制度展開諮詢。這些措施屬於降低海外投資人行政與稅務障礙的30項方案。因此，外資持有量創新高，既反映財政走向，也反映政府刻意提高本地債券交易便利性的努力。

俄羅斯的債券供給方向則相反。財政部長Anton Siluanov表示，2026年預算赤字將達GDP的3%，高於原計畫的1.6%及2025年的2.6%；1月至8月赤字已達GDP的2.5%。政府目前預期借款將超過原先規劃的5.5兆盧布、約合$657億，並將動用過往年度剩餘資金。

油價上漲與盧布走弱雖增加出口收入，仍未能阻止赤字擴大。俄羅斯央行表示，新預測符合其預期，高利率則已增加債務償付成本。Siluanov預計，國家財富基金準備金到年底將增加6,000億至1兆盧布，總額達約5兆盧布；但財政預測上修赤字，仍代表國內主權債發行將更加沉重。

加彭正準備2027年的大型對外籌資計畫。預算草案規劃從國際市場借入1.1兆非洲金融共同體法郎、約合$19億，並從國內或區域市場籌措6,000億非洲金融共同體法郎。國庫及融資資源總額預計由2026年的2.3兆增至2.9兆非洲金融共同體法郎，債務攤還額則達1.9兆。

政府審計把加彭2025年底債務存量估值由近11.7兆下修至9.5兆非洲金融共同體法郎，約相當於GDP的69%，但這項修正並未消除再融資負擔。加彭7月重返國際市場，發行$9.2億、7年期、定價殖利率9.375%的債券，目前一面清理未償負債，一面尋求新的IMF計畫。

委內瑞拉則為規模大得多的債務重整踏出早期制度性一步。由臨時總統Delcy Rodriguez率領的代表團在美國分別會見美洲開發銀行總裁Ilan Goldfajn、IMF總裁Kristalina Georgieva及世界銀行總裁Ajay Banga，討論債務重整、資金與付款，以及能源和礦業議題。

卡拉卡斯5月表示，將開始重整多數分析師估計總額達$1,500億至$2,000億的主權債與PDVSA債務。法律及財務顧問8月成立債權人委員會，協調持有未償債權的企業。美洲開發銀行正在準備一項2年期合作計畫，涵蓋電力、社會保障、總體經濟架構、資料及投資需求。這些會談尚未決定重整條款，但已使程序從廣泛宣告，向與多邊機構及有組織債權人實際接觸推進。

IMF與世界銀行另行批准修改雙方共同使用的低所得國家債務可持續性架構。新版將加強對國內債務、長期發展挑戰、預測及壓力測試的處理，折現率則維持5%。依IMF資料，約14%的低所得國家已陷入債務困境，另有33%處於高風險；約23%的新興經濟體則面臨整體主權壓力偏高的風險。

新版架構要到2027年下半年才會啟用。在評估過渡影響期間，塞內加爾仍將依現行方法受評；IMF也尚未說明新的國內債務處理方式可能如何影響該國重整。這項改革對未來債務承受能力分析相當重要，但本身不會改變當前債權人條款。

歐洲則面臨財政制度執行力的相關可信度問題。歐洲財政委員會警告，反覆使用彈性及豁免條款，正在削弱2024年4月通過的規則。依該制度，各國有4至7年時間使債務與赤字朝歐盟占GDP 60%及3%的上限調整，但目前尚未發出任何「遵守或解釋」聲明，只有保加利亞因新的過度赤字程序而面臨程序性後果。

歐盟政府債務占GDP比重由2024年的81%升至2025年的82%，歐洲執委會預計2026年將超過84%。國家豁免條款最早於2025年3月提出，之後先用於國防，再擴及部分能源韌性支出。委員會擔心，當政治成本上升時，反覆例外將削弱市場對調整計畫獲得執行的信心，進而提高未來債券供給與償債風險。

## 後續市場意義

9月22日美國市場的首項考驗，將前端美債供給與就業、製造業訊號集中在同一天。美國政府預定紐約時間下午1時標售$690億2年期公債。2年期殖利率目前為4.748%，週一並未跟隨其他天期上漲。標售需求將顯示，投資人是否認為目前殖利率足以補償市場預期聯準會緊縮約80個基點的風險，或在Goolsbee與Musalem示警後仍要求發行讓利。

ADP每週就業估值將於紐約時間上午8時15分公布，前值為16,250人；Richmond聯準銀行9月製造業指數於上午10時公布，市場共識為5，前值為4。芝加哥聯準銀行指數轉弱之際，政策官員仍認為需求與基礎通膨過強，使這些數據格外重要。招募與生產若轉弱，將強化週一的債券漲勢；經濟活動若持續擴張，前端則仍將承受終端利率上升的風險。

紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams也將發表演說，本週稍晚則由克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack接續發言。兩人的談話將協助判斷，Goolsbee願意接受經濟承受痛苦的立場，以及Musalem主張及早漸進升息的看法，是否代表更廣泛的委員會立場。Musalem並未明示下一步行動或最終利率高點，下一次升息時點因此仍取決於後續數據及現任投票委員的看法。

9月23日$700億5年期美債標售，將考驗週一殖利率下跌近3個基點、但近一個月仍上升逾40個基點的券種。同日也將公布S&P採購經理人指數初值；製造業預計由53.9降至53.5，服務業則由56.5降至56。數值若持續遠高於50，將支持聯準會對需求具有韌性的判斷；動能若更明顯流失，則會強化目前附近的實質殖利率已在抑制經濟活動的論點。

9月24日初領失業救濟金人數預計由196,000人升至203,000人。9月密西根大學消費者信心指數終值將於9月25日公布，市場共識為47.5，前值為51.7。勞動市場數據對政策的影響將高於信心數據本身，但兩者合併觀察，可顯示能源成本與高借款利率是否開始削弱家庭需求。

能源仍是週一債券漲勢最快可能反轉的途徑。海灣出口若進一步增加，且Trump與Pezeshkian會面，原油跌勢可能延續，並緩解損益兩平通膨率的壓力。攻擊若再起、油輪通行量進一步下降，或跡象顯示關閉應答器的運輸無法彌補商業航線受阻，通膨溢價便會回升。週末僅17艘可見船舶通行，戰前常態則約為每日125艘，兩者差距顯示實體運輸距離正常化仍相當遙遠。

習近平於9月23日至25日訪美期間舉行的Trump—習近平峰會，構成另一項成長與通膨事件。初步會談已同意建立AI對話，並讓涵蓋潛在非敏感商品的貿易委員會投入運作，但雙方都未公開確認延長關稅休戰。關稅、關鍵礦物及市場准入的具體條款，將決定關係改善能否降低貿易成本的不確定性，或只是把問題延後。

南非9月23日利率決策，將區分一次性的保險式升息與美國銀行預測的兩次升息序列起點。市場普遍預期升息25個基點至7.25%，但政策指引必須說明，通膨預期轉弱是否足以抵銷油價使整體通膨維持在5%附近的風險。奈及利亞與摩洛哥將於9月22日面臨類似決策；儘管存在進口能源與食品價格壓力，兩國均預計維持利率不變。

初級信用市場將直接顯示AI資本的價格。Digital Drive資料中心債券初步殖利率落在9%區間低端至中段，預計9月23日定價；SoftBank分為5批的美元及歐元債券則安排於9月24日定價。關鍵比較項目是最終殖利率、規模及到期年限配置：前者為有未來CoreWeave租約支持的興建專案籌資，後者則把部分OpenAI股權投資風險由過橋貸款銀行轉移至無擔保債券持有人。

AMC再融資將考驗入場人次與營收改善，能否支撐近$40億新融資的可持續總成本。Nuveen的英鎊與美元債券發行，則將顯示主權債殖利率仍高之際，市場吸收收購融資的能力。雖然美債較長天期部位上漲，整體高收益債利差大致持平，因此決定交易結果的仍是個別借款人的槓桿與結構，而非普遍的避險退潮。

對美債而言，核心問題在於油價衝擊緩解、但聯準會仍認為政策限制性不足的情況下，週一的多頭壓平能否延續。10年期殖利率低於5%、10年期實質殖利率為2.617%，加上風險資產需求強勁，顯示能源價格下跌時，市場可以消化鷹派政策路徑；2年期殖利率仍接近4.75%，則顯示市場尚未認定升息路徑已經完成。經濟數據、聯準會溝通及2年期標售，將決定前端最終能否加入漲勢，或把曲線其他部分重新拉向近期高點。

overall_summary.headline: 油價重挫帶動美債除前端外普遍上漲，聯準會示警使2年期殖利率維持高檔
overall_summary.session_narrative:
WTI下跌8.22%至$92.06，布蘭特原油下跌7.46%至$96.12，帶動美債除前端外普遍上漲。外交前景改善，加上海灣出口持續的跡象，降低眼前的供應稀缺溢價，使10年期殖利率下跌4.5個基點至4.952%，30年期下降4.2個基點至5.285%。2年期殖利率反而微升0.3個基點至4.748%，2年與10年期利差收窄4.8個基點至20.4個基點。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied beyond the front end on Sept. 21 as a severe daily drop in oil relieved some of the inflation pressure that had driven yields to multiyear highs, while Federal Reserve officials kept the policy-sensitive 2-year yield anchored near 4.75%. The 10-year yield fell 4.5 basis points to 4.952%, the 5-year declined 2.9 basis points to 4.828% and the 30-year dropped 4.2 basis points to 5.285%. The 2-year yield instead edged 0.3 basis point higher to 4.748%, flattening the 2s10s curve by 4.8 basis points to 20.4 basis points.

The move captured the distinction investors drew between immediate energy relief and the Fed’s longer policy problem. WTI futures fell 8.22% to $92.06 and Brent dropped 7.46% to $96.12 as diplomatic prospects and evidence that some Gulf exports were moving through the Strait of Hormuz weakened the scarcity premium. Yet visible traffic through the strait remained drastically below prewar norms, and Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee and St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem separately argued that persistent supply shocks could not simply be ignored. Musalem, a nonvoter this year, went further by describing the current 3.75%-4% federal-funds range as accommodative and saying additional increases were likely to be needed.

The Treasury rally came mainly through lower real yields. The 10-year inflation-adjusted yield fell 6 basis points to 2.617%, while the 10-year breakeven rose 1.5 basis points to 2.335%. That decomposition showed investors demanding less real compensation for holding duration as oil retreated, without concluding that the underlying inflation risk had disappeared. The Chicago Fed National Activity Index reinforced the softer growth side of the move, falling to -0.04 in August from a revised 0.08 and missing the 0.2 forecast.

Risk assets treated the fall in energy prices as relief rather than a warning about demand. The S&P 500 gained 1.49%, the Nasdaq 100 rose 2.83% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index surged 4.29% after early adoption of Meta’s Muse artificial-intelligence agent revived optimism about chip demand. High-yield credit spreads were little changed, while investment-grade, high-yield and emerging-market bond funds all posted positive daily returns. The combination made Monday a duration rally with strong risk appetite, not a flight from credit.

The session nevertheless left the front end carrying a demanding policy path. The 2-year yield has risen about 140 basis points from its February low, and futures imply roughly 80 basis points of additional Fed tightening over the coming year. Investors are beginning to argue that a yield near 4.75% already embeds much of that path, but Goolsbee and Musalem supplied reasons the market cannot yet treat the September increase as the end of the cycle. The result was a sharply differentiated close: lower oil and weaker activity supported intermediate and long Treasuries, while the prospect of further rate increases prevented the same relief at 2 years.

## Oil Relief Lowers Real Yields, but the Fed Keeps the Front End Firm

The daily Treasury move extended the curve flattening that followed the Fed’s first rate increase since 2023. The 2s30s spread narrowed 4.5 basis points to 53.7 basis points, taking its compression over the past month to almost 50 basis points. The 5-year yield remains 40.3 basis points higher over that period and the 2-year is up 51.1 basis points, even after longer maturities benefited from Monday’s rally. The market has therefore preserved a high expected path for overnight rates while reducing some of the compensation required farther out.

Oil was the clearest catalyst for the relief. Brent had been trading above $100 as the Iran war disrupted exports and complicated the inflation outlook, but it settled at $96.12 after a fourth consecutive decline. President Donald Trump said he would probably be open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during the UN General Assembly, while satellite observations indicated an increase in Saudi loadings from the Persian Gulf. The prospect that diplomacy and continued exports might improve availability helped lower the immediate energy premium in bonds.

The underlying physical picture was less reassuring than the futures move. Only 17 commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, down from 37 a week earlier and far below the roughly 125 large commercial vessels that typically passed through each day before the war began on Feb. 28. Trackable traffic does not capture the entire flow: 22 tankers, mostly very large crude carriers, carried 42 million barrels out of the strait in the week of Sept. 13, with Saudi Arabia and Iraq each accounting for 43% of that volume. Some tankers were traveling with transponders switched off.

That continuing flow helps explain why an extreme supply outcome was partly removed from prices, but the collapse in visible traffic leaves the energy route vulnerable to renewed disruption. There had also been no visible Saudi oil loadings from the Yanbu Red Sea port since Sept. 16. Monday’s oil decline therefore reduced the current inflation impulse without establishing that normal export capacity had returned.

Goolsbee’s speech addressed precisely that distinction. The Chicago Fed president said supply shocks had become more frequent, more severe and more persistent, weakening the traditional case for looking through them as one-time price-level changes. He argued that the Fed need not respond as aggressively as it would to an economy overheating through excess demand, but said restoring price stability could still require lower employment, wages and growth as policy narrows the gap between aggregate supply and demand.

That view places a different emphasis on the cost of disinflation from the one Chair Kevin Warsh presented after the September decision. Warsh said he did not believe the Fed’s employment and price-stability goals worked at cross purposes over the medium term and resisted the idea that returning inflation to 2% required harming the labor market. Goolsbee instead described a recurring negative supply shock as an inherently painful trade-off: once the shock lasts, monetary restraint must reduce demand even though the initial price increase originated elsewhere.

Musalem supplied a second and more explicitly hawkish policy signal later in the session. He said strong demand and recurring supply forces were both keeping inflation risks elevated and judged that, without further restraint, inflation was more likely to remain substantially above 2% in 18 months than return to target. Earlier, incremental increases would be less disruptive than waiting and then having to make larger moves, he said.

The St. Louis Fed president estimated that underlying inflation, excluding oil and other supply-related effects, was perhaps 1 percentage point above target and moving in the wrong direction. July personal-consumption-expenditures inflation was 3.7% from a year earlier, compared with a recent low of 2.3% in April 2025. His assessment that the 3.75%-4% policy range remained on the accommodative side was important because it did not rely solely on the oil shock. Musalem does not vote on the Federal Open Market Committee this year and did not identify the next meeting or terminal rate, but his preferred direction was clear.

The market’s response remained more nuanced than a simple rejection of those warnings. The 2-year yield held near its richest level since 2024, yet the 5- through 30-year sectors rallied as lower crude reduced the threat that the energy shock would force an even larger real-rate adjustment. At 4.748%, the 2-year also yields more than the roughly 4.68% policy rate implied by swaps for September 2027. That positive carry has attracted investors who believe the market already discounts another three increases and would benefit sharply if inflation improves or the Fed delivers fewer moves.

The counterargument is that hiking cycles have often gone farther than investors initially anticipated. Bank of America strategists have identified a risk that the policy rate ultimately exceeds 5%, particularly if officials continue to regard current settings as insufficiently restrictive. Oil can also reverse quickly if diplomacy fails or export routes deteriorate. Monday’s curve therefore reflected conditional relief, not confidence in a settled terminal rate.

The day’s economic release modestly favored duration. The Chicago Fed National Activity Index fell to -0.04 for August, below the 0.2 forecast and the revised 0.08 July reading. The index did not show a severe contraction, but it added to recent evidence that parts of production and broader activity were losing momentum even as consumption and labor conditions remained resilient.

Bill auctions showed that funding costs were still moving higher at the shortest maturities. The 3-month auction cleared at 4.015%, above 3.970% previously and the 3.9999% forecast. The 6-month bill auction stopped at 4.155%, up from 4.060%. Those results were consistent with a market that sees little prospect of near-term easing and continues to price policy tightening even while longer coupon yields decline.

## Global Central Banks Confront the Same Energy Shock at Different Starting Points

Canada, South Korea and South Africa supplied separate examples of how the energy shock is altering policy calculations outside the U.S. Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said officials did not want to restrain growth if inflation remained contained, but also did not want to wait until persistent pressure forced them to raise rates faster and farther. The question, he said, was whether the current 2.25% policy rate would return inflation to 2% or whether another increase was required.

Canadian headline inflation has remained around 3%, largely because of gasoline. Macklem said inflation would probably edge higher in coming months if oil stayed near $100. He also emphasized the risk that the effect broadens beyond fuel, rather than treating the initial energy increase itself as sufficient reason to tighten. The bank’s new Prima forecasting model will be used in its October monetary-policy report to distinguish temporary price changes from more persistent ones and to evaluate alternative scenarios.

Trade pressure complicates that assessment. Macklem said new U.S. tariffs directly affect products representing about 5% of Canada’s goods exports to the U.S., limiting the aggregate first-round effect. Their unpredictability could nevertheless delay investment and hiring, and he estimated that fourth-quarter growth could be roughly halved to below 1% if the tariffs remained in place. Canada’s dilemma is therefore not simply high inflation: an early hike risks amplifying a trade-related slowdown, while a late response could allow energy pressure to spread.

In South Korea, JPMorgan raised the prospect that the policy-rate peak could exceed its already above-consensus forecast. The bank expects quarter-point increases in November, February and May, taking the Bank of Korea’s rate from 3% to 3.75%, compared with a 3.5% median forecast that remains unchanged through Q2 2028. The central bank’s August projections implied only one additional increase over six months.

JPMorgan economist Seok Gil Park tied the upside risk to the semiconductor boom. He expects the economy to grow 3.8% in 2026 and 3.3% in 2027, above the BOK’s 3.3% and 2.9% forecasts. For Q3, JPMorgan projects growth of about 1% from the prior quarter, versus the central bank’s estimate of roughly 0.3%. Business investment has already benefited, but whether chip earnings spread through suppliers, wages and household demand will determine how persistent the inflation effect becomes.

The won’s appreciation reduces imported costs, yet it is not unambiguously disinflationary if it reflects better terms of trade and stronger real income. Park is watching core manufactured goods excluding petroleum and personal services, where monthly price gains have remained elevated. The BOK is expected to hold on Oct. 22, making its October statement and November forecasts the next tests of whether officials place more weight on the boom’s domestic spillovers.

South Africa faces a nearer decision on Sept. 23. Morgan Stanley changed its call from a hold to a 25-basis-point increase to 7.25%, describing the move as insurance against repeated supply shocks delaying inflation’s return to the South African Reserve Bank’s 3% target. Its case is not based on a present deterioration in inflation expectations or evidence that energy pressure has already spread widely through consumer prices. Rather, prolonged oil inflation would lower the real policy rate and raise the chance that expectations eventually become unanchored.

Bank of America expects an even longer sequence, with quarter-point increases in September and November taking the repo rate to 7.5%. It raised its forecast for Q4 inflation to an average of 5% and expects a 5.3% peak in Q1 2027. That call contrasts with Morgan Stanley’s expectation that one increase will be followed by unchanged rates through 2027. Surveyed inflation expectations have actually eased to 3.8% from 3.9%, leaving the disagreement centered on how aggressively the central bank should insure against oil before second-round effects appear.

The same tension extends across Africa. Seven of 11 central banks meeting over the following two weeks were expected to hold, three to raise rates and one to cut. Nigeria was expected to keep its rate at 26.5% for a third meeting, despite room created by earlier disinflation, because recent fuel-price increases could reverse the trend. Morocco was expected to hold at 2.25%, while Egypt could retain a 19% rate through year-end. Energy and food carry unusual weight across the region, where food represents as much as half of some consumer-price baskets and a powerful El Niño threatens harvests.

India’s bond market faced a related tightening through liquidity rather than only the policy rate. Its benchmark 10-year government yield ended the prior week at 7.0686%, its fifth consecutive weekly increase, after rising 5 basis points during the week and about 26 basis points over the preceding four. The Reserve Bank of India had sold 500 billion rupees of shorter-dated government bonds, its first net auction sale since 2017, and had scheduled another 250 billion-rupee sale for Sept. 21 and a further 250 billion rupees the following Monday.

The operations are withdrawing cash created after banks raised $127 billion through a special foreign-exchange mobilization scheme. That inflow left the banking system in surplus and pushed overnight rates below the policy corridor floor. Bond sales therefore serve a monetary-control purpose, but they also add supply and pressure duration while traders are raising their expectations for a policy-rate increase.

China moved in the opposite currency direction. The onshore yuan reached 6.6950 per dollar, its strongest level since January 2023, and closed at 6.6955, its strongest domestic close since June 2022. The People’s Bank of China set its midpoint at 6.7487, the strongest fixing since February 2023. The fixing remained 536 pips weaker than the Reuters estimate, but its faster appreciation during September and the narrowing gap with market expectations suggested that officials were becoming more tolerant of gradual yuan strength.

## AI Financing Tests the Depth and Price of Credit Demand

SoftBank converted a prospective megadeal into a defined financing, launching $10 billion of dollar senior unsecured notes and €1 billion, about $1.15 billion, of euro debt. At the planned size, it would be the largest Asia-Pacific and Japan nonfinancial corporate bond offering on record, surpassing 7-Eleven’s $10.93 billion sale in January 2021.

The dollar offering is divided among 3.5-, 5.5- and 7.5-year maturities, while the euro debt has 4- and 6-year tranches. Pricing is expected on Sept. 24 and settlement on Sept. 29. Proceeds will finance a $10 billion third-tranche payment for SoftBank’s follow-on investment in OpenAI, expected to close Oct. 1, and general corporate purposes. The bonds will replace a previously secured $10 billion bridge facility.

The scale makes the transaction more than another example of abundant primary-market liquidity. SoftBank has committed close to $65 billion to OpenAI and sold almost $15 billion of notes across currencies during 2026, making it the year’s largest junk-rated bond borrower. The yield on its dollar bond due in 2031 rose to 8.2% earlier in September from 6.7% in January as both Treasury yields and its credit spread increased. Fitch rated the proposed notes BB+, matching the highest speculative-grade category assigned to the company by S&P.

The structure shifts part of SoftBank’s OpenAI exposure from secured bridge funding into unsecured public debt, broadening its maturity profile but placing more of the investment risk with bondholders. OpenAI’s decision not to pursue an initial public offering this year delays one potential source of liquidity for SoftBank’s holding. The final pricing will show how much compensation investors require for that concentration after a year of unusually heavy AI-related borrowing.

A separate data-center financing illustrated the cost of construction exposure. Banks led by Goldman Sachs began marketing about $1.1 billion of junk bonds for the Digital Drive project near Richmond, Virginia, sponsored by affiliates of Blue Owl Capital, Cedarwood Investment Group and PowerHouse Data Centers. Early discussions indicated a low- to mid-9% yield, with pricing expected Sept. 23.

The project’s 76 megawatts of information-technology capacity will be fully leased to CoreWeave under a 15-year, $2.94 billion contract, with operations expected to start between 2027 and 2028. The lease supplies a visible revenue stream, but investors still face construction, completion and tenant-credit risks before the facility becomes operational. Its indicated yield shows that a long contract with an AI customer provides access without eliminating the premium attached to an unfinished project.

Fidelity International portfolio manager James Durance identified the aggregate growth of technology debt as a risk in itself. He has kept technology exposure below 2% across income strategies overseeing $14 billion and argued that the sector’s borrowing could become systemically significant by the end of 2027. A global technology-debt gauge has lost about 2.4% over the past year, compared with a 1.3% decline for the broader global aggregate index. His concern is not that AI investment must fail, but that long-duration debt issuance is expanding before companies have demonstrated whether enormous capital commitments will earn adequate returns.

The same capital intensity is influencing monetary-policy analysis. ECB Governing Council member Fabio Panetta said market valuations embed optimistic assumptions about AI profitability and could correct sharply if those expectations are disappointed. He estimated that broad AI adoption could lift Italian productivity growth by more than 1 percentage point annually, while stressing that its inflation effect depends on who receives the gains. Higher expected income could strengthen consumption and sustain inflation; automation and job uncertainty could instead raise saving and bring disinflation sooner.

Monday’s equity move emphasized the optimistic scenario. Meta’s Muse became the leading free application in Apple’s App Store, helping Meta shares rise 11%, Advanced Micro Devices gain 10% and exceed $1 trillion in market value, Intel climb 12% and Arm advance 17%. The rally improved the market backdrop for AI financing, but it also underscored how much equity valuations, corporate borrowing and investment spending increasingly depend on the same technology cycle.

Credit demand was not confined to AI. AMC Entertainment launched a $2 billion junk-bond offering and an $850 million leveraged loan and obtained a commitment from Deutsche Bank for a $1.12 billion second-lien loan, seeking almost $4 billion to overhaul its capital structure. The bonds were initially offered at a yield in the low-9% area.

AMC intends to repay term loans due in 2029 and 2031 and notes issued by AMC and Muvico that mature in 2029. The refinancing follows a failed attempt six months earlier, when poor market conditions forced the company to rely on a $425 million transaction with Deutsche Bank’s distressed-products unit. Its improved access rests on a box-office recovery: July and August revenue rose 42% from a year earlier to $1.33 billion, while attendance increased 36%. AMC still had $3.7 billion of corporate borrowings at June 30, leaving execution and the resulting interest burden central to the transaction.

Qatar demonstrated a much stronger sovereign funding position despite suffering direct damage from the war. The government raised $3 billion in its first public international bond sale since November, pricing 5-year notes at 55 basis points over Treasuries and 10-year debt at 65 basis points. Both spreads tightened about 30 basis points from initial indications. Orders peaked above $7.7 billion before easing to about $6.8 billion.

Demand reflected Qatar’s AA rating, $580 billion sovereign wealth fund and more than $70 billion of foreign-exchange reserves. Those buffers coexist with an abrupt deterioration in current revenue. LNG export receipts fell to $200 million in Q2 from $9 billion in Q1 as Hormuz disruption constrained shipments, while the quarterly budget deficit reached a record $5.8 billion, or 11.4% of GDP. The transaction showed that strong accumulated assets can preserve funding access even when the operating shock is severe.

Nuveen was also preparing its first sterling bond alongside three dollar issues to finance part of its £9.9 billion acquisition of Schroders. The planned sterling maturity is 5 years, and proceeds will support general corporate purposes including cash consideration for the purchase. Nuveen had already arranged a debt facility of as much as £3.1 billion. Together with SoftBank, AMC and the Digital Drive project, the pipeline showed borrowers using a constructive market day to address very different financing needs, with terms varying sharply according to leverage, collateral and execution risk.

## Sovereign Funding Rewards Credibility and Penalizes Fiscal Drift

Chile recorded one of the clearest examples of foreign demand following a credible fiscal and market-development program. Nonresident holdings of peso-denominated sovereign bonds increased by $700 million in August to a record $21.04 billion, taking the gain since the start of 2026 to 42%. Foreign investors held 15.6% of the local sovereign market in March, nearly double the 8% share at the end of 2024.

The flows coincided with a 95 billion-peso budget surplus in July, compared with a 957 billion-peso deficit a year earlier. Private mining revenue rose 79%, spending declined 0.7% and year-to-date expenditure increased only 0.7%. Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz plans to limit spending growth to between zero and 1% next year, strengthening the contrast with fiscal deterioration elsewhere in Latin America.

Market reforms have supported the allocation. Chile is seeking to let pension funds conduct repo and reverse-repo transactions, which could improve financing and secondary-market liquidity, and has opened consultation on a market-maker program. The initiatives are part of 30 measures intended to reduce paperwork and tax barriers for overseas investors. The record holdings therefore reflect both the fiscal trajectory and a deliberate effort to make local bonds easier to trade.

Russia presented the opposite supply direction. Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said the 2026 budget deficit would reach 3% of GDP, compared with a 1.6% plan and 2.6% in 2025. The January-August shortfall had already reached 2.5% of GDP. The government now expects to borrow more than the initially planned 5.5 trillion roubles, or about $65.7 billion, and use leftover funds from prior years.

Higher oil prices and a weaker rouble have increased export revenue but have not prevented the deficit from widening. The central bank said the new projection was consistent with its expectations, while high interest rates have increased debt-servicing costs. Siluanov expects National Wealth Fund reserves to rise by 600 billion to 1 trillion roubles to about 5 trillion by year-end, but the fiscal revision still implies heavier domestic sovereign issuance.

Gabon is preparing a large external funding program for 2027. Its draft budget calls for 1.1 trillion CFA francs, about $1.9 billion, of international borrowing and 600 billion CFA francs from domestic or regional markets. Total treasury and financing resources are projected to rise to 2.9 trillion CFA francs from 2.3 trillion in 2026, while debt amortization reaches 1.9 trillion CFA francs.

A government audit reduced the estimate of Gabon’s end-2025 debt stock to 9.5 trillion CFA francs from almost 11.7 trillion, putting it near 69% of GDP. That revision did not eliminate the refinancing burden. The country returned to international markets in July with a $920 million, 7-year bond priced at 9.375% and is seeking a new IMF program while clearing outstanding liabilities.

Venezuela took an early institutional step toward restructuring a much larger debt stock. A delegation led by interim President Delcy Rodriguez met separately with Inter-American Development Bank President Ilan Goldfajn, IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva and World Bank President Ajay Banga in the U.S. Discussions focused on debt restructuring, funds and payments as well as energy and mining.

Caracas said in May that it would begin restructuring sovereign and PDVSA obligations estimated by most analysts at $150 billion-$200 billion. Legal and financial advisers formed a creditor committee in August to coordinate companies with outstanding claims. The IDB is preparing a 2-year engagement plan that includes work on electricity, social protection, the macroeconomic framework, data and investment needs. The meetings do not determine restructuring terms, but they move the process from a broad announcement toward engagement with multilateral institutions and organized creditors.

The IMF and World Bank separately approved changes to their joint debt-sustainability framework for low-income countries. The revision will strengthen the treatment of domestic debt, long-term development challenges, forecasting and stress testing, while leaving the discount rate at 5%. About 14% of low-income countries are already in debt distress and another 33% are at high risk, according to IMF data, while about 23% of emerging economies face high overall sovereign-stress risk.

The revised framework will not become operational until H2 2027. Senegal will continue to be assessed under the existing approach while transition implications are considered, and the IMF has not specified how the new treatment of domestic debt could affect its restructuring. The reform is therefore important for future debt-capacity analysis, but it does not change current creditor terms by itself.

Europe faces a related credibility issue in the enforcement of its fiscal regime. The European Fiscal Board warned that repeated use of flexibility and escape clauses was weakening rules adopted in April 2024, which give countries 4 to 7 years to move debt and deficits toward the EU’s 60% and 3%-of-GDP limits. No comply-or-explain statements had been issued, and only Bulgaria had faced procedural consequences through a new excessive-deficit process.

EU government debt increased to 82% of GDP in 2025 from 81% in 2024, and the European Commission expects it to exceed 84% in 2026. National escape clauses were first offered in March 2025, then used for defense and later for some energy-resilience spending. The board’s concern is that repeated exceptions raise future supply and debt-service risk by weakening confidence that adjustment plans will be enforced when political costs rise.

## Forward Market Significance

The first U.S. test on Sept. 22 combines front-end Treasury supply with labor and manufacturing evidence. The government is scheduled to sell $69 billion of 2-year notes at 1 p.m. New York time. The auction arrives with the 2-year yield at 4.748%, after the maturity failed to participate in Monday’s broader rally. Demand will show whether investors regard the current yield as sufficient compensation for roughly 80 basis points of expected Fed tightening or still require a concession after Goolsbee and Musalem’s warnings.

ADP’s weekly employment estimate is due at 8:15 a.m. New York time after 16,250 previously. The Richmond Fed’s September manufacturing index follows at 10 a.m., with consensus at 5 after 4. These releases matter because the Chicago Fed index weakened while policymakers continued to describe demand and underlying inflation as too strong. Evidence of softer hiring and production would reinforce Monday’s duration rally; continued expansion would leave the front end exposed to a higher terminal-rate path.

New York Fed President John Williams is also scheduled to speak, followed later in the week by Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack. Their remarks will help establish whether Goolsbee’s acceptance of economic pain and Musalem’s call for earlier incremental tightening represent a broader committee position. Musalem did not specify either the next step or the eventual peak, leaving the timing of another move sensitive to incoming data and the views of current voters.

The $70 billion 5-year Treasury auction on Sept. 23 will test a sector that rallied almost 3 basis points on Monday but remains more than 40 basis points higher over the past month. Flash S&P purchasing-manager indexes arrive the same day. Manufacturing is expected at 53.5 after 53.9 and services at 56 after 56.5. Continued readings well above 50 would support the Fed’s assessment of resilient demand; a sharper loss of momentum would strengthen the case that real yields near current levels are already restraining activity.

Initial jobless claims on Sept. 24 are expected at 203,000 after 196,000. The final September Michigan sentiment reading follows Sept. 25, with consensus at 47.5 against 51.7 previously. The labor data will carry more policy weight than confidence alone, but the combination can reveal whether energy costs and high borrowing rates are beginning to weaken household demand.

Energy remains the quickest route to a reversal in Monday’s bond rally. Further increases in Gulf exports and a Trump-Pezeshkian meeting could extend the decline in crude and relieve pressure on breakevens. Renewed attacks, another fall in tanker traffic or evidence that transponder-dark shipments cannot compensate for disrupted commercial routes would restore the inflation premium. The gap between 17 visible weekend transits and the prewar norm of about 125 vessels a day shows how much physical normalization is still required.

The Trump-Xi summit during Xi Jinping’s Sept. 23-25 U.S. visit creates a separate growth and inflation event. Preliminary meetings produced an agreement to establish an AI dialogue and operationalize a Board of Trade covering possible nonsensitive goods, but neither side publicly confirmed an extension of the tariff truce. Concrete terms on tariffs, critical minerals and market access will determine whether the improved tone reduces trade-cost uncertainty or merely postpones it.

South Africa’s Sept. 23 rate decision will distinguish a one-time insurance increase from the beginning of the 2-hike sequence forecast by Bank of America. A 25-basis-point rise to 7.25% is widely expected, but the guidance must address whether softer inflation expectations outweigh the risk of oil keeping headline inflation near 5%. Nigeria and Morocco face similar decisions on Sept. 22, with both expected to hold despite imported energy and food pressure.

Primary credit will provide direct evidence on the price of AI capital. The Digital Drive data-center bond is expected to price Sept. 23 after indications in the low- to mid-9% area. SoftBank’s 5-tranche dollar and euro transaction is scheduled for pricing Sept. 24. The relevant comparisons are the final yield, size and maturity allocation: one deal funds a construction project supported by a future CoreWeave lease, while the other transfers part of an equity investment in OpenAI from bridge lenders to unsecured bondholders.

AMC’s refinancing will test whether improved attendance and revenue can support almost $4 billion of new financing at a sustainable all-in cost. Nuveen’s sterling and dollar sales will show how readily acquisition debt can be distributed while sovereign yields remain elevated. These transactions arrive in a market where broad high-yield spreads were little changed even as Treasury duration rallied, leaving borrower-specific leverage and structure—not a general risk retreat—to determine execution.

For Treasuries, the central issue is whether Monday’s bull flattening can persist when the oil shock is easing but the Fed still regards policy as insufficiently restrictive. A 10-year yield below 5%, a 10-year real yield of 2.617% and strong demand for risk assets show that markets can absorb a hawkish policy path when energy prices fall. The 2-year yield near 4.75% shows that they have not yet concluded the path is complete. Data, Fed communication and the 2-year auction will determine whether the front end finally joins the rally or pulls the rest of the curve back toward the recent highs.

Russia’s wider deficit implied heavier domestic issuance, while Gabon planned substantial 2027 borrowing despite a lower audited debt stock. Venezuela began engaging multilaterals and organized creditors, and future sovereign assessments will face a revised IMF-World Bank framework and renewed concern over weakened European fiscal enforcement.

U.S. Treasury auctions, labor and activity data, and Fed speeches will test whether the front end can join the rally or pull longer yields back toward recent highs. Gulf exports and Hormuz traffic remain the fastest route to a reversal in oil and breakevens. The Trump-Xi summit will test whether improved engagement reduces trade-cost uncertainty, while South Africa’s decision and AI-related bond pricing will reveal how policy and credit markets absorb the energy and investment shocks.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally beyond the front end as oil tumbles, while Fed warnings keep 2-year yields firm
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied beyond the front end as WTI fell 8.22% to $92.06 and Brent dropped 7.46% to $96.12. Diplomatic prospects and evidence of continued Gulf exports reduced the immediate scarcity premium, helping the 10-year yield fall 4.5 basis points to 4.952% and the 30-year yield decline 4.2 basis points to 5.285%. The 2-year yield instead edged 0.3 basis point higher to 4.748%, flattening the 2s10s curve by 4.8 basis points to 20.4 basis points.

The rally came mainly through lower real yields: the 10-year real yield fell 6 basis points to 2.617%, while the 10-year breakeven rose 1.5 basis points to 2.335%. The Chicago Fed National Activity Index also softened to -0.04, but Goolsbee and Musalem warned that persistent supply shocks could not simply be ignored. Musalem called the 3.75%-4% policy range accommodative and said further increases were likely to be needed.

Risk assets treated cheaper energy as relief rather than a demand warning. Equities rallied sharply on renewed AI optimism, while U.S. high-yield spreads were little changed. The close therefore combined a duration rally and strong risk appetite, with the front end still constrained by roughly 80 basis points of expected Fed tightening and uncertainty over whether Gulf exports can normalize.
overall_summary.summary: A sharp oil decline and weaker activity data lowered real yields across intermediate and long Treasuries, but officials’ warnings that persistent supply shocks may require further tightening left the policy-sensitive 2-year yield near 4.75%.
